name: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)
description: Reliable, ordered, byte-stream transport over IP. RFC 793. Connection-oriented (3-way handshake SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK; 4-way close FIN/ACK/FIN/ACK). Flow control via receive window; congestion control via cwnd (Reno/Cubic/BBR). The default for HTTP, SSH, most application protocols. Linux implementation surfaces in tcp(7) man page; tunable via setsockopt with SOL_TCP / TCP_* options and sysctls under net.ipv4.tcp_*.

name: UDP (User Datagram Protocol)
description: Connectionless message-oriented transport. RFC 768. No reliability, ordering, or congestion control — sender writes a datagram, kernel sends one packet. DNS queries, NTP, QUIC's underlying transport, RTP, syslog over UDP. Per-message-boundary semantics; recvfrom returns one datagram. Linux: udp(7) man page; SO_RCVBUF/SO_SNDBUF still apply.

name: IPv4
description: Version 4 Internet Protocol. 32-bit addresses (4.3 billion). Header includes TTL, fragmentation, ToS, source/dest. Linux IPv4 stack in net/ipv4/. ip(7) covers BSD-socket interface; sysctls under net.ipv4.* tune behavior.

name: IPv6
description: Version 6 Internet Protocol. 128-bit addresses, simplified header, no fragmentation by routers (path MTU discovery), built-in IPsec support. Linux IPv6 stack in net/ipv6/. ipv6(7) man page; net.ipv6.* sysctls.

name: ICMP / ICMPv6
description: Internet Control Message Protocol. RFC 792 (v4) / RFC 4443 (v6). Carries diagnostic and error messages: echo request/reply (ping), destination unreachable, time exceeded (TTL=0, used by traceroute), redirect, fragmentation needed. Not a transport in the BSD-sockets sense — opened via raw sockets.

name: Unix domain sockets
description: Local IPC over the filesystem. Stream (SOCK_STREAM), datagram (SOCK_DGRAM), or seqpacket (SOCK_SEQPACKET) semantics. Identified by a filesystem path (or abstract namespace prefixed with \0). Faster than TCP loopback (no IP/transport-layer overhead). Used by Docker socket /var/run/docker.sock, DBus, systemd, X11.

name: Netlink
description: Bidirectional kernel↔userspace message channel. Family AF_NETLINK. Subprotocols include NETLINK_ROUTE (interface/route mgmt — what `ip` uses), NETLINK_NETFILTER (nftables, conntrack), NETLINK_AUDIT, NETLINK_GENERIC. Replaces ioctl as the modern way to manage kernel networking subsystems.

name: Packet (raw layer-2) sockets
description: Family AF_PACKET. Direct access to layer-2 frames, bypassing the IP stack. Used by tcpdump (libpcap), wireshark, DHCP clients (need to send before having IP), and anything implementing its own L2 protocol. PF_PACKET socket types: SOCK_RAW (full ethernet), SOCK_DGRAM (cooked, no eth header).

name: Raw IP sockets
description: Family AF_INET/AF_INET6 with type SOCK_RAW. Lets userspace assemble and send IP packets with custom headers. Requires CAP_NET_RAW. Used by ping, traceroute (when implemented as raw rather than ICMP), nmap.

name: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol)
description: Maps IPv4 addresses to MAC (Ethernet) addresses on a local link. RFC 826. Request: 'who has 10.0.0.5?' broadcast; reply: 'I do, MAC=...'. ARP cache (`ip neigh show`) per-netns. Stale or poisoned entries break L3 connectivity even when L1/L2 are fine.

name: NDP (Neighbor Discovery Protocol, IPv6)
description: IPv6 equivalent of ARP. Uses ICMPv6 messages (Neighbor Solicitation, Neighbor Advertisement, Router Solicitation, Router Advertisement). Also handles router discovery and SLAAC.

name: DNS
description: Domain Name System. Hierarchical name → record (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SOA, PTR, SRV) lookup. Default UDP/53 (TCP/53 for AXFR/large responses), DoT TCP/853, DoH HTTPS/443. Linux client-side: glibc's resolver (configured via /etc/resolv.conf), nsswitch (which DBs to consult), or systemd-resolved.

name: Ethernet (L2)
description: Layer-2 frame format. 6-byte src+dst MAC, optional 802.1Q VLAN tag, EtherType (0x0800 IPv4, 0x86dd IPv6, 0x0806 ARP, 0x88cc LLDP), payload, FCS. The default L2 on every Linux interface; bridges connect ethernet segments at L2.

name: VLAN (802.1Q)
description: Layer-2 segmentation via 4-byte tag inserted between MAC and EtherType. 12-bit VID (0-4095). Linux: `ip link add link eth0 name eth0.10 type vlan id 10`. Each VLAN gets its own subinterface; bridges can forward by VID.

name: VXLAN
description: Virtual eXtensible LAN. L2-over-UDP overlay (default UDP/4789). 24-bit VNI (16M virtual networks). Used by Docker overlay driver, Kubernetes Calico/Flannel for pod networking across nodes.

name: GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation)
description: L3 tunneling protocol (IP protocol 47). Encapsulates arbitrary L3 in IP. Linux: `ip tunnel add gre0 mode gre remote ... local ...`. Used in some VPN setups and SDN underlays.

name: IPsec
description: IP security suite (AH for authentication, ESP for encryption+auth). Tunnel or transport mode. Linux: XFRM framework configured via `ip xfrm`. Strongswan/wireguard-go alternatives common.

name: TLS
description: Transport Layer Security. RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3). On TCP. Provides encryption + authentication + integrity. Linux's KTLS offload (CONFIG_TLS) does symmetric crypto in-kernel for sendfile() throughput. Most application TLS is in userspace via OpenSSL/GnuTLS.

name: DHCP
description: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol. UDP/67-68. Client broadcasts DISCOVER → server OFFER → client REQUEST → server ACK. Linux clients: dhclient, dhcpcd, systemd-networkd's built-in DHCP. Container-runtime IP allocation usually IPAM (Docker/CNI), not DHCP.

name: TCP state: LISTEN
description: Server socket waiting for incoming SYN. Created by listen(2). `ss -tln` shows; `ss -tlpn` adds owning PID. Backlog queue depth from listen()'s 2nd arg, capped by net.core.somaxconn.

name: TCP state: SYN_SENT
description: Client has sent SYN, awaiting SYN-ACK. If kernel retries (net.ipv4.tcp_syn_retries) elapse without response, connect() returns ETIMEDOUT.

name: TCP state: SYN_RECV
description: Server received SYN, sent SYN-ACK, awaiting client ACK. SYN-cookie protection avoids per-half-open-conn allocation under SYN flood (net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies).

name: TCP state: ESTABLISHED
description: Bidirectional data flow possible. Where the bulk of socket lifetime is. `ss -t` shows.

name: TCP state: FIN_WAIT_1
description: Local side sent FIN; awaiting remote's ACK or remote's FIN. After local close().

name: TCP state: FIN_WAIT_2
description: Local FIN ACKed; awaiting remote's FIN. Stuck connections here usually mean remote app hasn't closed.

name: TCP state: TIME_WAIT
description: Active closer waits 2*MSL (~60-120s on Linux) before fully releasing the 4-tuple. Prevents delayed segments from a previous incarnation polluting a new connection. High TIME_WAIT count = client-side process making many short connections; tune via tcp_tw_reuse, ephemeral port range, or app-level connection pooling.

name: TCP state: CLOSE_WAIT
description: Remote sent FIN; local has ACKed but local app hasn't called close(2). Stuck in CLOSE_WAIT = file-descriptor leak in local app.

name: TCP state: CLOSED
description: Connection fully torn down. The kernel removes the socket entry. Briefly visible in /proc/net/tcp before cleanup.

name: Socket type SOCK_STREAM
description: Reliable byte-stream socket. Implies TCP for AF_INET/AF_INET6, stream-style for AF_UNIX. read()/write() may return short — caller must loop.

name: Socket type SOCK_DGRAM
description: Message-boundary preserving socket. Implies UDP for AF_INET; datagram unix-socket for AF_UNIX. Each recv() returns at most one datagram (truncates if buffer too small).

name: Socket type SOCK_RAW
description: Raw socket — packet-level access. Requires CAP_NET_RAW. AF_INET SOCK_RAW = raw IP; AF_PACKET SOCK_RAW = raw L2.

name: Socket type SOCK_SEQPACKET
description: Sequenced, reliable, message-boundary preserving (best of stream + datagram). Used by AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET.

name: Address family / protocol family
description: socket(2)'s first arg. AF_INET (IPv4), AF_INET6 (IPv6), AF_UNIX/AF_LOCAL (unix domain), AF_NETLINK (kernel ↔ user), AF_PACKET (raw L2), AF_BLUETOOTH, AF_CAN (CAN bus). Determines address layout and protocol choice constraints.

name: Port binding
description: bind(2) attaches a socket to a local address+port. Without explicit bind, kernel picks an ephemeral (net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range). Privileged ports (<1024) require CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE. EADDRINUSE if already bound; EADDRNOTAVAIL if address not on a local interface.

name: Connection establishment (3-way handshake)
description: client SYN → server SYN-ACK → client ACK. Then both sides ESTABLISHED. connect(2) on the client returns when ACK arrives (or timeout). accept(2) on the server returns the new socket once the third ACK arrives.

name: Connection teardown (4-way handshake)
description: close(2) → FIN → ACK from peer → peer's close → FIN → ACK. Both sides traverse FIN_WAIT_1/FIN_WAIT_2/CLOSE_WAIT/LAST_ACK/TIME_WAIT depending on who closed first. Half-closed state via shutdown(2) SHUT_WR.

name: Ephemeral port range
description: net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range — port range kernel picks for outbound connections that didn't explicitly bind. Default ~32768-60999. Exhaustion → connect() returns EADDRNOTAVAIL.

name: Path MTU Discovery
description: Sender starts with interface MTU; routers may reply ICMP 'fragmentation needed' with the next hop's MTU. Linux records discovered MTU per route. Broken if intermediate firewalls drop ICMP — black-hole problem manifests as 'small packets work, large hang'. tcp_mtu_probing sysctl enables a fallback probing mechanism.

name: TCP window scaling
description: RFC 1323 option allowing the 16-bit receive-window field to be scaled by a factor (up to 14). Required for high-bandwidth-delay-product links. net.ipv4.tcp_window_scaling=1 default. NAT or middlebox stripping the option breaks throughput on long-RTT links.

name: TCP congestion control
description: Algorithm choosing send rate to avoid network collapse. Linux ships reno, cubic (default since 2.6.19), bbr, dctcp, vegas, illinois. Per-socket override via TCP_CONGESTION sockopt; default via net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control. Default 'cubic' is good general-purpose; 'bbr' wins on bufferbloat-prone paths.

name: TCP keepalive
description: After tcp_keepalive_time idle (default 7200s), kernel sends probes every tcp_keepalive_intvl (default 75s). After tcp_keepalive_probes failures (default 9), connection is reset. Per-socket override via SO_KEEPALIVE + TCP_KEEPIDLE/TCP_KEEPINTVL/TCP_KEEPCNT.

name: TCP Fast Open
description: RFC 7413. Carries application data in the SYN packet, eliminating one RTT for repeat connections. Server replies with a TFO cookie in SYN-ACK; subsequent connections from same client present the cookie to authenticate early-data. net.ipv4.tcp_fastopen sysctl (1=client, 2=server, 3=both).

name: TCP SYN cookies
description: net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies. When the SYN queue overflows (under SYN flood), encode connection state into the SYN-ACK ISN — no per-half-open allocation. Slight performance penalty, immune to half-open SYN floods. Default 1 since Linux 2.4.

name: SO_REUSEADDR vs SO_REUSEPORT
description: REUSEADDR: bind() doesn't error if same address is in TIME_WAIT or different-but-overlapping (wildcard vs specific). REUSEPORT (Linux 3.9+): MULTIPLE listening sockets can bind the SAME port — kernel load-balances incoming connections across them via 4-tuple hash. The high-throughput accept() pattern.

name: Nagle's algorithm vs TCP_NODELAY
description: Nagle (default ON) buffers small writes until previous data is ACKed, reducing tinygram overhead. Hurts latency-sensitive small-write workloads. TCP_NODELAY=1 disables Nagle. TCP_CORK is opposite — actively coalesce until uncorked. SSH, interactive protocols set NODELAY; bulk transfer benefits from default.

name: TCP_CORK
description: Linux-specific. While set, kernel buffers writes (up to ~200ms) before sending. Useful when you'll write multiple small chunks and want them coalesced into one segment. Common pattern: SET_CORK → sendfile + write_header → CLEAR_CORK.

name: Netfilter hook chain
description: Per-protocol-family chain of hook points: PREROUTING, INPUT, FORWARD, OUTPUT, POSTROUTING. Packets traverse hooks in fixed order; iptables/nftables register rules at hook points. Knowing the chain order is essential for understanding why a rule didn't match.

name: iptables table
description: Tables group rules by purpose: filter (default — ACCEPT/DROP/REJECT), nat (DNAT/SNAT/MASQUERADE), mangle (TOS/TTL/marks), raw (NOTRACK before conntrack), security (SELinux integration). Each table has its own copy of relevant chains.

name: iptables chain
description: Per-table linear list of rules. Built-in chains: INPUT (to local), OUTPUT (from local), FORWARD (transit), PREROUTING (before routing), POSTROUTING (after routing). User-defined chains for grouping. Default policy applies if no rule matches.

name: iptables match-and-target
description: Rule = match criteria (-p, -s, -d, --sport, --dport, -i, -o, --state, --syn, etc.) + jump target (-j ACCEPT/DROP/REJECT/LOG/MASQUERADE/...). First matching rule's target executes (unless target returns).

name: SNAT (Source NAT)
description: Rewrites the source IP/port of outbound packets at POSTROUTING. e.g. private 10.0.0.0/8 → public IP. MASQUERADE is the auto-pick-source variant (for dynamic IPs like DSL/cable).

name: DNAT (Destination NAT)
description: Rewrites the destination IP/port at PREROUTING. The mechanism behind 'docker -p 8080:80' (incoming :8080 → container :80). Conntrack remembers the original tuple so reply packets get rewritten back.

name: Conntrack (connection tracking) table
description: Per-namespace table of all flows kernel is tracking. Required for stateful filtering (`-m state ESTABLISHED,RELATED`) and NAT (so reply packets get reverse-translated). nf_conntrack_max bounds size; full table = new connections drop. `conntrack -L` lists; `cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack` raw.

name: Conntrack timeouts
description: Per-protocol per-state timeouts. nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established = 5 days default — too short for keepalive-less long-lived TCP connections through firewalls. ESTABLISHED expiring kills the conn for the firewall but not for endpoints (resulting in RST when traffic resumes).

name: nftables family
description: Top-level grouping. inet (IPv4+IPv6 unified), ip (IPv4 only), ip6 (IPv6 only), arp, bridge, netdev (per-interface ingress/egress at lowest level). 'inet' is the modern default for dual-stack rules.

name: nftables table → chain → rule hierarchy
description: nft rule lives in a chain, which lives in a table (in a family). Chains hook into netfilter (type filter/nat/route, hook input/output/forward/prerouting/postrouting, priority N). Rules within evaluated top-down. More flexible than iptables fixed schema.

name: nftables sets and maps
description: Named sets store discrete values (IPs, ports, MACs); maps store key→value. Lookup is O(log n) (red-black tree backend). Replaces the iptables ipset hack. Allows e.g. `ip saddr @blocklist drop` against a dynamic set updated from userspace.

name: Routing table
description: Per-netns set of routes. Linux supports multiple tables (named in /etc/iproute2/rt_tables, indexed 0-255). Default 'main' (254) holds normal routes; 'local' (255) holds local interface addresses; rules in `ip rule` decide which table to consult per packet. `ip route` shows; `ip route get <dst>` evaluates.

name: Policy routing (ip rule)
description: Per-packet route-table selection by source/destination/fwmark/iif/oif. `ip rule add from 10.0.0.0/8 lookup 100`. Enables multi-homing with per-source default routes.

name: veth pair
description: Virtual ethernet — pair of back-to-back interfaces. Packet in one comes out the other. The standard mechanism for connecting a network namespace to the host (one end stays in host bridge, other end goes into the netns). Created via `ip link add type veth peer name ...`.

name: Bridge (Linux bridge)
description: In-kernel L2 switch. Multiple interfaces attached as ports; bridge learns MACs and forwards frames. STP optional (off by default). docker0, virbr0 are bridges. bridge(8) configures STP/VLAN-filtering/per-port settings beyond what `ip link` exposes.

name: TAP / TUN devices
description: Userspace ↔ kernel virtual interfaces. TUN: L3 (IP packets); TAP: L2 (Ethernet frames). OpenVPN/WireGuard use TUN (route packets to userspace VPN process); QEMU uses TAP (give VM an L2 interface).

name: Bonding (link aggregation)
description: Combine multiple NICs into one logical interface for HA or throughput. Modes: active-backup, balance-rr, balance-xor, 802.3ad (LACP), broadcast, balance-tlb, balance-alb. Configured via `ip link add bond0 type bond` + per-slave attach.

name: tc qdisc
description: Queueing discipline — algorithm controlling order/timing of packet transmission on an interface. pfifo_fast (default for older kernels), fq_codel (modern default — fairness + bufferbloat reduction), htb (hierarchical token bucket — for rate limits), cake (modern fq+aqm). Configured via tc qdisc add. (Detail in linux/networking-advanced; tc(8) man page is bulky enough that we don't ingest it in this leaf — see Phase 1.5).

name: epoll edge-triggered vs level-triggered
description: EPOLLET = edge-triggered: events fire ONCE on state change; you must drain the socket fully (until EAGAIN) before re-entering epoll_wait. Level-triggered (default) keeps firing while data is pending. ET is more efficient at scale but trickier — most application-server bugs in this area are ET-related.

name: epoll vs select/poll
description: select/poll have O(N-monitored-FDs) per call. epoll registers FDs once (epoll_ctl) and returns only those with events (epoll_wait). For thousands of long-lived connections, epoll is dramatically faster.

name: net.core.somaxconn (listen-queue ceiling)
description: Hard ceiling on the SOMAXCONN argument to listen(2)'s backlog. App passes a value; kernel min(app-value, somaxconn). If somaxconn is too low, accept queue overflows during connection bursts → connections dropped (visible as ListenOverflows in /proc/net/netstat).

name: SO_RCVBUF / SO_SNDBUF
description: Per-socket receive/send buffer size in bytes. Auto-tuning in modern kernels (tcp_rmem/tcp_wmem range). Setting to small value can cap throughput on long-RTT links (BDP > buffer = stall).

name: glibc resolver
description: libresolv: reads /etc/resolv.conf at first lookup, caches. Honors search domains, options (timeout, attempts, single-request, ndots, edns0, rotate). nsswitch.conf decides which databases (files, dns, mdns) and order. Most processes use it transparently via getaddrinfo(3).

name: systemd-resolved
description: Local DNS stub on 127.0.0.53. Caching, DNSSEC, DoT support, multi-NIC awareness (per-link DNS). nsswitch entry 'resolve' or symlink /etc/resolv.conf → /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf. resolvectl(1) inspects.

name: resolv.conf 'ndots' option
description: Threshold for relative-vs-absolute name lookups. ndots=N: if a query has fewer than N dots, try search-list suffixes first. Default 1. Kubernetes' default ndots=5 explodes lookup count for FQDN-like internal names — common source of surprise DNS latency.

name: netfilter subsystem
description: Kernel framework for packet filtering, NAT, mangling. Provides the hook points; iptables and nftables are userspace tools that program rules at those hooks. Per-netns rule tables (so each container has its own iptables view).

name: iptables subsystem
description: Legacy userspace tool + kernel modules (xt_*, ipt_*) for netfilter rule programming. Mature, ubiquitous, but linear-scan rule lookup. Being replaced by nftables but still ships everywhere.

name: nftables subsystem
description: Modern netfilter front-end. Single CLI (nft), unified inet family for v4+v6, sets/maps with O(log n) lookup, atomic ruleset replace. Default on RHEL 8+, Debian 11+. iptables-nft compat layer exists.

name: conntrack subsystem
description: nf_conntrack module. Tracks every flow's state for stateful filtering and NAT. Per-netns table. Tunable via sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_*.

name: BSD socket API subsystem
description: socket(2)/bind(2)/listen(2)/accept(2)/connect(2)/send(2)/recv(2)/close(2)/setsockopt(2)/getsockopt(2)/shutdown(2). The interface every networking application uses. Implementations per address family.

name: iproute2 (ip command suite)
description: User-space tool suite (`ip`, `ss`, `tc`, `bridge`, `nstat`) replacing the older net-tools (ifconfig, route, netstat, arp). Talks to kernel via NETLINK_ROUTE. Only sane interface for IPv6, multiple routing tables, policy routing.

name: DNS resolver subsystem (NSS+resolv)
description: Userspace stack: glibc's nsswitch dispatcher → per-DB modules (files, dns via libresolv, resolve via systemd-resolved). Determines name → address resolution for getaddrinfo(3).

name: epoll subsystem
description: Scalable I/O readiness notification. epoll_create1(2), epoll_ctl(2), epoll_wait(2). Per-CPU red-black trees of monitored FDs. The basis of every modern Linux event loop (libuv, libev, tokio).

name: firewalld / ufw / shorewall
description: Higher-level firewall managers built on iptables/nftables. firewalld (zone-based, RHEL/Fedora default). ufw (uncomplicated, Ubuntu default). shorewall (declarative). Each generates lower-level rules; mixing with raw iptables can fight.

name: socket(2) syscall
description: Create an endpoint for communication. Returns a FD. Args: domain (AF_*), type (SOCK_*), protocol (usually 0 = default for type).

name: bind(2) syscall
description: Assign a local address+port to a socket. Required before listen() (server) or for clients wanting a specific source.

name: listen(2) syscall
description: Mark a stream socket as passive (server). Backlog arg sets the SYN+accept queue depths (kernel uses min(backlog, somaxconn)).

name: accept(2) / accept4(2) syscall
description: Dequeue a completed connection from the listen-socket's accept queue, returning a new connected socket. Blocks if queue empty (unless O_NONBLOCK). accept4 adds flag arg (SOCK_NONBLOCK, SOCK_CLOEXEC) — race-free atomic alternative to accept+fcntl.

name: connect(2) syscall
description: Initiate a connection. For TCP, sends SYN, blocks for handshake (or returns EINPROGRESS if O_NONBLOCK). For UDP, sets default destination so subsequent send() works.

name: send(2)/recv(2)/sendto/recvfrom/sendmsg/recvmsg
description: Data transfer. send/recv on connected sockets; sendto/recvfrom carry per-call destination/source; sendmsg/recvmsg pass scatter-gather + ancillary data (SCM_RIGHTS for FD passing over AF_UNIX, IP_PKTINFO for source-address selection).

name: setsockopt(2)/getsockopt(2) syscalls
description: Per-socket option get/set. Args: socket FD, level (SOL_SOCKET, IPPROTO_TCP, IPPROTO_IP, IPPROTO_IPV6), option name, value buffer. Where SO_REUSEADDR / TCP_NODELAY / IP_BIND_ADDRESS_NO_PORT etc. are set.

name: shutdown(2) syscall
description: Half-close a socket. SHUT_RD (no more reads), SHUT_WR (no more writes — sends FIN), SHUT_RDWR (both). Distinct from close() which releases the FD entirely.

name: epoll_create1/epoll_ctl/epoll_wait syscalls
description: epoll_create1 makes an epoll instance (FD); epoll_ctl adds/modifies/deletes monitored FDs; epoll_wait blocks until events or timeout. The Linux high-performance event loop primitive.

name: poll(2)/select(2)/pselect
description: Older readiness-multiplexing syscalls. Pass a list of FDs each call (vs epoll's persistent registration). poll() uses pollfd struct (no FD_SETSIZE limit); select() is bit-mask based and limited to FD_SETSIZE (1024). pselect adds atomic sigmask swap.

name: NETLINK_ROUTE driver
description: netlink subprotocol for interface/route/neighbor/qdisc/filter management. The thing `ip` and `tc` talk to. Notifications also flow back (interface up/down, address add/remove, route change).

name: NETLINK_NETFILTER driver
description: netlink subprotocol for nftables, conntrack, ulogd. nft uses it to install rulesets; conntrack(8) uses it to query/modify the conntrack table.

name: Linux bridge driver
description: In-kernel L2 switch implementation. Forwards frames between attached interfaces. MAC learning, STP, VLAN-filtering modes. Heart of docker0 and most VM networking.

name: bonding driver
description: Link aggregation. Loaded as bonding module. Mode + per-mode params via /sys/class/net/bondN/bonding/* or systemd-networkd's [Bond] section.

name: TUN/TAP driver
description: Universal virtual interface. Userspace process opens /dev/net/tun, configures via TUNSETIFF ioctl, then read/write packets. Used by VPNs, VMs, container userspace networking (slirp4netns).

name: /proc/net/tcp{,6}
description: All IPv4 (and v6) TCP sockets, with state, local/remote addr, queue depths, owning UID, inode. Read by ss(8) and netstat. Hex-encoded; ss does the decoding for you.

name: /proc/net/udp{,6}
description: UDP sockets enumeration. Same shape as /proc/net/tcp.

name: /proc/net/unix
description: Unix-domain sockets. Lists Inode + RefCount + Protocol + Flags + Type + State + Path. ss -x parses.

name: /proc/net/dev
description: Per-interface byte/packet counters (rx/tx, errors, drops, fifo, frame). What ifconfig and `ip -s link` parse. drops > 0 = receive ring overflow, often hint that net.core.rmem_max needs raising or NIC driver tuning.

name: /proc/net/route
description: Hex-encoded IPv4 routing table. `route` parses (deprecated); `ip route` uses NETLINK_ROUTE instead.

name: /proc/net/arp
description: IPv4 ARP cache. `arp -a` parses. Modern equivalent: `ip neigh show`.

name: /proc/net/snmp
description: Per-protocol counters in SNMP-MIB names: TcpExt (tcp extended stats), TcpInSegs, TcpRetransSegs, IpInDelivers, etc. nstat(8) parses to a friendly form. Source of TCP retransmit %, listen-queue-overflow counters.

name: /proc/net/netstat
description: Extended counters not in /proc/net/snmp. ListenOverflows (full accept queue), ListenDrops, TCPSynRetrans, TCPLossUndoUuse, etc. Read by `nstat -as`.

name: iptables -m state / -m conntrack
description: Stateful filtering. -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED accepts return traffic and conntrack-related packets (FTP data conn, ICMP errors). The cornerstone of 'allow established' firewall rules.

name: iptables -m recent
description: Per-IP rate-limit / temporary blocklist within iptables. e.g. SSH brute-force protection: count attempts per IP, drop when threshold exceeded for a window.

name: iptables -m limit
description: Token-bucket rate limit on rule match. e.g. log only 5 packets/sec to avoid log flooding.

name: nftables 'meta' selector
description: Match on packet metadata: meta iif/oif (interface), meta mark (fwmark), meta priority (skb priority), meta length, meta nftrace, meta cgroup (cgroup ID).

name: nftables 'ct' (conntrack) selector
description: Match on conntrack state: ct state established/related/new/invalid; ct status; ct mark.

name: tcpdump BPF filter expression
description: libpcap filter language compiled to cBPF for in-kernel packet matching. Syntax: `host`, `port`, `src`, `dst`, `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `ip`, `ip6`, boolean operators. Used by tcpdump, wireshark, raw libpcap apps.

name: tcpdump -w to pcap file
description: Capture to a .pcap file for offline analysis (wireshark, tshark, tcpdump -r). Combined with -C (size rotate) and -W (file count) for ring-buffer captures.

name: SO_BINDTODEVICE
description: Bind a socket to a specific interface name (e.g. 'eth0'). Bypasses normal routing — packets only on that interface. Requires CAP_NET_RAW. Used by VPN clients to send packets out a specific tunnel.

name: IP_BIND_ADDRESS_NO_PORT
description: Defer port assignment from bind() to connect(). Lets bind() reserve a source IP without consuming an ephemeral port — the kernel picks per-destination at connect() time, allowing far more concurrent outbound connections to a single dest:port. Critical for high-fanout proxies.

name: SO_MARK / fwmark
description: Per-packet 32-bit mark stored in skb->mark. Set per-socket via SO_MARK (requires CAP_NET_ADMIN), or via iptables/nft 'meta mark set'. Used by policy routing (`ip rule add fwmark X lookup Y`).

name: net_cls cgroup (v1)
description: Per-cgroup network class id, written to skb->priority for tc filters. v1 only — v2 uses BPF cgroup hooks instead. Largely obsolete in modern container setups.
